historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not distinguish the M.2 board's management sideband from PCIe/NVMe data-path identity and may probe unrelated controllers.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds M.2 population, temperature and NVMe health evidence, but the absent spec still leaves the actual board, sideband endpoints, safe registers and acceptance undefined.
historical_reviews.history: Round-2 retained this exact row UNRESOLVED; no M2_BD sideband map or approved criterion was found.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The project rule treats I2C as BMC/platform scope by default, so a Linux adapter scan does not prove access to the required M.2 board.

original_test_intent: Validate the M.2 board's platform-management I2C/SMBus sideband devices and correlate them with the installed M.2/NVMe population without affecting storage presence, data path or power state.
original_method: No bus operation is authorized until the owner defines the M.2 board/revision, populated slots/devices, BMC mux route, sideband addresses/registers, expected responses and storage-safe recovery, followed by fresh review.
manual_activity: Storage/platform owners must identify M2_BD and populated slots, document its BMC sideband topology and approve non-disruptive registers plus storage-health recovery.
required_inputs: NVMe presence, namespace and health acceptance
safety_requirements: Do not scan all host adapters
Do not equate PCIe/NVMe discovery with M.2 sideband validation
Do not probe unknown EEPROM, sensor, power or control registers
Do not use force or write-capable I2C operations
Preserve active storage and health evidence
Stop on device disappearance, reset, temperature, media, BMC or bus anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Perform no I2C scan or storage operation
Do not borrow E1.S or cable topology
engineer_actions: Approve M2_BD revision and populated slot map
Define BMC route and safe sideband register allowlist
Set M.2/NVMe correlation and health criteria

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The global i2cdetect loop neither selects M2_BD nor correlates responders to physical M.2 slots and NVMe identities. It can touch storage-sideband control endpoints, suppresses errors and truncates evidence, with no check for device disappearance or reset.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: define the M.2 sideband topology, slot population and safe register oracle before selecting a command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The literal I2C M2_BD scope and two-minute estimates are preserved; no slot, bus, address, register or NVMe device is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After approval, use the owning BMC/OOB route to read only allowlisted inventory/temperature/status fields for each populated M.2 slot, bind responses to device serial/firmware and compare pre/post NVMe presence, namespaces, SMART/health and BMC events.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Establishes slot and sideband identity plus storage-health correlation instead of host-wide address discovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An I2C response does not prove which M.2 slot or NVMe device it represents, while NVMe enumeration does not prove the platform-management sideband path.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: M.2 boards may combine EEPROM, sensors and power/reset controls; an incorrect transaction can disturb a live storage device, so target identity and independent recovery are required.

project_override_considerations: Treat M2_BD I2C as BMC/platform-management scope and require exact controller/mux/address/register mapping plus storage-device correlation and expected output.
expected_evidence: Approved M2_BD specification and fresh review
Board/revision, slot, M.2/NVMe serial/firmware and BMC controller/mux identity
Allowlisted sideband transactions with complete raw responses
Response-to-slot/device mapping and expected inventory/temperature/status values
Pre/post NVMe presence, namespace, SMART/health, kernel and BMC SEL/SDR evidence
No reset/data-path impact plus abort/recovery audit and owner verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row is not contradictory, but the referenced procedure and criterion are absent, leaving target and acceptance undefined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Storage-sideband identity and safe transaction semantics are unknown. Package installation or confirmation cannot establish whether a responder belongs to M2_BD or whether probing can affect storage availability.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1809 Wistron-HW-00011-V003 I2C M2_BD: board/revision and populated M.2 slot/device mapping, BMC/OOB controller and mux path, sideband address/device/register allowlist, reserved power/reset controls, expected responses and NVMe presence/health criteria, aborts and independent storage recovery; preserve Master placeholders and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Separates the M.2 platform-management sideband from the PCIe/NVMe data path and makes slot/device correlation and storage availability part of the blocking contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: M.2 storage can expose management information through a platform sideband that is distinct from NVMe enumeration. A global I2C scan cannot map a response to a slot or prove the data path stayed healthy, and an unknown endpoint may include power or reset controls. The absent specification therefore prevents both safe targeting and a meaningful PASS oracle.
